$comment: Source of truth for the models the web app loads. Editing this file is how you deploy a
retrained model - no JavaScript changes needed. Drop the .onnx next to this file, update
`file`, `labels` and `imgsz` to match what you exported, and the app picks it up.
A model whose `file` is missing or fails to load is reported in the UI as unavailable;
the app stays usable for whatever else did load. Keep every file well under ~15 MB - it
downloads to the visitor's browser. Export with `python3 tools/export_onnx.py`, which
`ondevice` is not one of the trained detectors. It is a COCO model that ships with the
app and finds people and vehicles with no key and no connection; see DETECTOR.md for
what that does and does not cover, and why it is this model rather than a YOLO one.

gate.description: Routes an upload to the right analysis, or rejects it.

turbine.notes: No model. Blade damage is the one subject here nobody appears to have published weights for: the conversion workflow searched the model index for wind turbine blade damage, defect detection, crack detection and inspection, and every search came back empty. That is a fact about what exists rather than a fault in the fetching. Until somebody publishes some, this subject needs a provider key, which describes a frame in words instead of boxing what is in it.
turbine.zeroDetectionNote: Nothing was marked, because there is no blade model to mark anything with. This is not a reading about the blade.

solar.notes: Fetched already trained rather than trained here. It knows bird droppings, dust, snow, physical damage and a general defective class, and it also knows what an undamaged panel looks like, which is dropped before anything is drawn so a healthy panel is not boxed as a finding. RGB only, so it cannot show hotspots, cell defects, bypass-diode failure or an offline module: those are electrical faults visible only in thermal infrared, and no amount of daylight resolution reaches them.
solar.zeroDetectionNote: None of the visible-light defect classes were found in this frame. RGB cannot show hotspots, cell defects, bypass-diode failure or an offline module, so a frame with nothing marked says nothing about those.

crowd.notes: Trained on aerial imagery, so a figure a few pixels tall seen from above is what it was built for rather than what it struggles with. It also knows vehicles, and they are dropped before overlapping boxes are resolved, so a van standing beside someone can never suppress the person. Read the tally, not the band: people carry no severity, and the band scores only the pressure patterns the provider engine describes. The tally is of the boxes in this frame, which is not the same as everyone present: anyone hidden behind someone else is one box, and a figure smaller than a few pixels is not marked at all.
crowd.zeroDetectionNote: No figure in this frame passed the threshold. That is a null result about one frame at one moment, not a reading about the place: at altitude a person can be too few pixels across to mark, and someone under a tree, a canopy or a vehicle cannot be seen from above at all.

wildfire.notes: A detector trained on fire and smoke, which is a stronger thing than the colour and movement scan the live view runs, and a blunter one: it has a single class and cannot say which of the two it is looking at. The live view still separates them, from how a region behaves over time, and still runs when this is not loaded. One frame from one angle either way. Fire behind a smoke column, inside a treeline or under canopy does not appear from above, and a person the camera cannot resolve is the normal case rather than a rare one.
wildfire.zeroDetectionNote: Nothing was marked in this frame. That describes this frame and nothing else: not the ground under the smoke, not what is inside the treeline, and not whether anyone is there. A fire too small or too far to hold a region is not marked, and neither is one the smoke above it is hiding.

ondevice.notes: Two engines, side by side. A COCO detector finds people and vehicles. Flame and smoke are computed from colour and from how the region behaves over time rather than from a trained model, so they are candidate regions for an operator to confirm, not a verdict. Cracks, corrosion and soiling are outside both engines and still need a provider model.
ondevice.zeroDetectionNote: Nothing was marked in this frame. This engine looks for people, vehicles, flame colour and smoke; damage to a structure is outside what it knows. A person a few pixels across, which is what a person is from altitude, is the case it misses first, and a fire too small or too far to hold a region will not be marked either. Treat an empty frame as a frame that needs a look, not as a reading about the scene.

firescan.notes: Flame is flame colour that changes on most frames rather than holding still, which is what separates a fire from a red vehicle or a sunset. Smoke is a desaturated region that drifts and veils the texture behind it. A single photograph carries no motion, so a still is capped below the confidence a stream can earn.
